report_ready.primary_comparison: The ICES1991 Rpath port remains the whole-North-Sea validation target, but fresh direct diagnostics on the explicitly documented nonfeeding structural-zero runtime with EE floor0.1 return FAIL for GE, TE and With Egestion. GE and With Egestion have divergent recycling and negative detrital-source contributions; TE has no negative entries but fails PP balance. The former East Coast Scotland1991–1995 candidate has saved GE OK and TE FAIL, and about39.55% target overlap. Neither model has researcher approval. These are different source/runtime configurations; the current result does not establish source/native equivalence or production eligibility.
report_ready.scotland_mapping: The retained Scottish appendix covers all 384 current total-catch labels, including zero-catch taxa. Its 2019 catch and independent simple-chain inputs agree with the current regional data: 2,717,260.698205 t catch and 188,909,420.829195 t C simple-chain PPR. Of 384 taxa, 372 have saved mappings and 12 freshwater labels remain unresolved. High-confidence decisions account for 92.0810% of simple-chain PPR; Very low decisions account for 3.8483% (12.0072% of catch), and unresolved labels for 0.003350% (0.002334% of catch). Seventy-two labels lack a classic coefficient but all have zero 2019 catch, so no positive-catch PPR is unknown. The retained source-landings/biomass proxy allocations assume transfer from Scottish 1991–1995 conditions to the larger region, other years and total catch including discards. These saved decisions are candidate-specific and do not supply the current ICES model mapping.
report_ready.selection_recommendation: For interim computation, prefer the modern East Coast Scotland1991–1995 candidate because its retained GE and With Egestion diagnostics pass; TE remains failed. This is a provisional recommendation: approximately39.55% regional footprint, historical transfer assumptions and unknown snapshot execution provenance limit reuse. Keep the presently selected ICES model as a whole-region development target; its tested current adapted runtime fails all three direct configurations. No selection change or researcher approval is made.
report_ready.ICES_GE: FAIL. The living network converges (rho_living = 0.289443), but detritus recycling diverges (b = 1.555280) and the PP balance gap is 78.818%. There are 132 negative source/group entries: DetritusDOMWaterColumn [67] affects every consumer [1–65] plus pool [67]; DetritusPOMSediment [68] affects every consumer [1–65] plus pool [68]. Full recipient names and exact values are retained in the linked negative-entry table. Detritus SPPR: pool67 −0.153723; pool68 −0.435596; Discards69 0.
report_ready.ICES_TE: FAIL. No negative SPPR entries across the complete 70×5 basal-source matrix. The living network converges (rho_living = 0.573446); b = 0 is the method's convention. PP balance fails with a 78.818% relative gap. Detritus SPPR is zero for all three pools (67–69); source/loader routing limitations remain.
report_ready.ICES_runtime_limitations: The original standard-loader calls all stopped at a technical exception: four undefined imported-diet cells on nonfeeding basal rows prevented their basal-source columns from being formed. The reported run treats only those four cells as operational zeros on a separate runtime copy. Source missingness is unchanged. It uses EE floor 0.1 (8 living groups; hypothetical nonfishery sink 1.983704 t/km²/y). The loader still omits producer routing, forces detritus self-routing and resets source TL. Runtime detritus residuals are −609.876807, −806.816060 and −0.495862 t/km²/y for pools67–69; these do not replace the source BioAcc=0 observations or establish missing supply. All three returned configurations fail; no annual results or scientific approval are established.
report_ready.comparison_configuration_limit: The two diagnostic packages use different documented runtime histories, so this is an evidence-based suitability comparison, not a controlled comparison under identical calculation assumptions.
